title: DTCR consumer bootstrap profile
description: The immutable thin-binding bootstrap profile a new or existing repository adopts to be bound to this procedure. It is a profile, not an engine: the applying machinery is `shared-skills-infra`'s already-tested `consumer_bootstrap.py` / `repository_control_plane.py attach`, named here by path rather than reimplemented, because a second applier for one consumer is the duplicate-authority pattern CORE-LAW-001 and CORE-LAW-006 forbid. Two properties are structural rather than advisory. The `preconditions` array exists so that a binding this repository cannot legally perform today is a *represented state* with an owner, instead of an omission a reader fills in with optimism; the checker reconciles each declared state against the observed tree in both directions, so neither a papered-over block nor a stale block survives. And `terminal_scope` fixes what the declared terminal may never be read as: a committed profile is not an executed bootstrap, and an executed bootstrap is not a consumer that ever ran a review.

issue.description: The issue this artifact discharges. Fixed, because a profile that can be re-attributed to another issue can be counted as evidence for one it was never authored against.

terminal_scope.description: Written as constants so overclaiming is unrepresentable here rather than discouraged elsewhere. The three false entries are the whole reason this object exists: the terminal above names a profile that is ready to be applied, and a reader who never sees these will read it as a repository that was bootstrapped.

subject_pin.description: The exact skills-shared subject a consumer binds to. Every field is resolvable by `git rev-parse` in this repository, which is what stops a pin from being typed rather than observed: an invented or abbreviation-expanded SHA does not resolve, and a tree moved without its commit does not match.

repository.description: Opaque `owner/name` identity of the canonical repository. Not a clone URL: a URL names one host and one access path, and reads downstream as a locator someone may fetch.

repin_policy.description: What a later repin must move together, and what a partial repin would silently produce.

control_plane_profile.description: A `repository-control-plane-profile/v1` document, embedded verbatim rather than restated in a second vocabulary. It is deliberately NOT typed by this schema: the checker validates it against the committed `skills/shared-skills-infra/references/repository-control-plane-profile.v1.schema.json`, so this profile and the engine that will consume it cannot drift apart while both stay green on their own.

bootstrap_engine.description: The already-admitted machinery that applies this profile. Named by path so the reuse is checkable; every path is asserted present by the checker, because an engine reference that has rotted reads exactly like one that works.

generated_consumer_surface.description: The machine authorities the engine writes into a consumer. Consumer-relative, and asserted by the checker against the engine's own path constants, so this list cannot describe a surface the engine stopped generating.

superseded_consumer_surface.description: Paths a reader might expect from elsewhere and that this profile deliberately does not generate. Recorded rather than omitted: an omitted alternative gets reinvented by the next Worker, who has no way to see that it was considered and refused.

preconditions.description: What must hold before any consumer may be bound to this profile. Each entry's `state` is reconciled against the tree by the checker in both directions, so a block cannot be papered over and a lifted block cannot be left standing.

observed_by.description: Where the checker reads the observed value. A precondition whose state nothing reads is a promise.

state.description: `SATISFIED` only when the tree says so. `HUMAN_ADMIT_REQUIRED` is a person's decision no machine may make on their behalf; `NOT_IMPLEMENTED` is work nobody has done. They are not interchangeable, because the first cannot be discharged by a Worker and the second cannot be discharged by an admission.

attach_observation.description: The engine's own answer, executed rather than predicted. While any precondition is unsatisfied the engine must refuse this profile and `refusal_message` must be the exact text it raised; once every precondition is satisfied the engine must accept it and `refusal_message` must be null. Both directions are asserted, which is what turns `blocked` from prose into an exit the checker read.

residuals.description: Lanes this artifact does not close. Each carries the issue that owns it, so a residual has somewhere to go instead of decaying into an unowned caveat.

then.description: Permanently outside this issue. No profile, however green, establishes that a repository was bootstrapped and reviewed.
Admission of a Skill into the shared registry is a person's act. A Worker recording it under a general directive is the safety failure this field exists to keep unrepresentable.

authority.description: Constants, so a profile cannot widen what a profile is allowed to do.

sha1.description: Exact object name. A branch, tag, HEAD, `latest` or an abbreviation names a moving or ambiguous object, and a binding dated to one is dated to nothing.

repo_relative_path.description: Repository-relative. An absolute path, a home-relative path, a URI scheme or a parent traversal describes a location on one machine rather than a place in a tree.
